Hi Sophie / team — Laura from Legal. I reviewed the tracked changes and drafted three inline options in the attached doc (see section 9, Limitation of Liability):

1) Baseline (Redwood standard): Cap = aggregate of fees paid in the 12 months prior to the claim. Carve-outs = (a) willful misconduct, (b) fraud, (c) IP indemnity, (d) breach of confidentiality, (e) death/bodily injury, (f) statutory/regulatory fines where permitted by law. Excludes consequential, special, incidental damages.

2) Middle ground (compromise): Cap = greater of $500k or 2x fees paid in the prior 12 months. Same carve-outs as baseline. For consequential damages, retain the exclusion but add an explicit exception for direct regulatory penalties that the customer is legally obligated to pay to a third party as a direct consequence of Redwood’s breach.

3) Customer-friendly: Cap = 2x total fees paid under the Order Form during the 12-month measurement; add an annual-reset formula to limit run-rate exposure. Broader carve-outs for required regulatory fines and third-party IP claims where Redwood is adjudicated liable.

Notes / legal tradeoffs:
- Multiples vs absolute: Multiples (e.g., 2–3x) are commercial but expose Redwood to tail risk in very high-spend customers.
- Annual vs total-contract: Annual/rolling windows limit Redwood’s exposure growth over long contracts but can be gamed if the customer front-loads consumption.
- Carve-outs: We will defend IP indemnity and confidentiality carve-outs strongly; adding an explicit willful-misconduct exception is standard.

I tracked the three language options in the doc and flagged the places where we need negotiation (cap number, window, specific carve-outs). Mateo — I called out commercial fallback language if Nimbus insists on a 2x cap; suggest we offer the "middle ground" as our initial concession.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Quick commercial note — customer is sensitive to any cap that looks like a fixed low-dollar amount. Nimbus is in health and has regulatory exposure; they will push for carve-outs for fines. Our preferred play is: offer middle ground (2x fees or $500k floor) with annual reset and explicit carve-out for regulatory fines limited to statutory/regulatory bodies (not third-party punitive damages). If they press on multiples, negotiate for a 3x multiplier only if they commit to a minimum annual spend threshold or a dedicated capacity clause in the Order Form.

Also recommend we create a short ops checklist for the customer success + SRE teams if we accept a broader carve-out: 1) incident triage SLAs; 2) logs/audit export timelines; 3) rollback/fallback commitments; 4) evidence preservation for indemnity. I can draft that for the call.

— Karthik
Head of Business Development, Redwood Inference
